profile.summary: LAMAR is an RNA language model from the Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health (CAS) for studying how RNA processing is regulated. It reads an RNA sequence one nucleotide at a time and returns an embedding for each nucleotide; fine-tuned versions predict splice sites, translation efficiency from 5' UTRs, mRNA degradation from 3' UTRs and internal ribosome entry sites (IRES). It was pre-trained on about 15 million genome and transcript sequences from 225 mammals and 1569 viruses.

summary_quotes.text: LAMAR was developed by Rnasys Lab and Bio-Med Big Data Center, Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health (SINH), Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS).
LAMAR takes the RNA sequence as input and represents the nucleotides and RNAs.
LAMAR is fine-tuned to predict the splice site, mRNA translation efficiency, mRNA degradation rate and internal ribosome entry site (IRES).
LAMAR is pretrained on approximately 15 million sequences from both genome and transcriptome of 225 mammals and 1569 viruses

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: LAMAR is a bidirectional Transformer encoder with 12 layers, each with 12 attention heads and a feed-forward size of 3072, and rotary position embeddings. Each nucleotide is one token. During pre-training a portion of nucleotides (15%) is masked and the model predicts them from the surrounding sequence. The code builds the model with an ESM-style model class, EsmModel, from the repository's own LAMAR package. For a downstream task, a task-specific prediction head is placed on the final embeddings and the model is fine-tuned, either with the encoder frozen or with all parameters updated.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two pre-trained models exist: LAMAR-2k (context up to 2048 tokens) and LAMAR-4k (up to 4096 tokens), each saved at training step 250,000. Four fine-tuned models are also published: SpliceSitePred, UTR5TEPred, UTR3DegPred and IRESPred. All six sit in one Hugging Face repository, zhw-e8/LAMAR, as safetensors files under folders named for the run, so a result should give the folder name and the Hugging Face revision. The README's embedding example passes the architecture as arguments that override the base configuration file, which describes a different ESM-2 model (30 layers, hidden size 640); a user must keep those overrides.

steps.title: Compute embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from LAMAR.modeling_nucESM2 import EsmModel
from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoTokenizer
from safetensors.torch import load_file, load_model
import torch


seq = "ATACGATGCTAGCTAGTGACTAGCTGATCGTAGCTG"
model_max_length = 1026
device = torch.device("cuda:0")
# instance tokenizer and config
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("tokenizer/single_nucleotide/", model_max_length=model_max_length)
config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(
    "config/config_150M.json", vocab_size=len(tokenizer), pad_token_id=tokenizer.pad_token_id,
    mask_token_id=tokenizer.mask_token_id, token_dropout=False, positional_embedding_type='rotary',
    hidden_size=768, intermediate_size=3072, num_attention_heads=12, num_hidden_layers=12
)
# intance the model and load pretrained weights
model = EsmModel(config)
weights = load_file('pretrain/saving_model/mammalian80D_4096len1mer1sw_80M/checkpoint-250000/model.safetensors')
weights_dict = {}
for k, v in weights.items():
    new_k = k.replace('esm.', '') if 'esm' in k else k
    weights_dict[new_k] = v
model.load_state_dict(weights_dict, strict=False)
model = model.to(device)
# Compute embeddings
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    inputs = tokenizer(seq, return_tensors="pt")
    input_ids = inputs['input_ids'].to(device)
    attention_mask = inputs['attention_mask'].to(device)
    outputs = model(
        input_ids=input_ids,
        attention_mask=attention_mask
    )
    embedding = outputs.last_hidden_state[0, 1 : -1, :]
print(embedding.shape)
PY

limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The example sets model_max_length to 1026 although LAMAR-4k was pre-trained with 4096-token contexts; the README does not explain the choice.
The tokenizer and configuration are read from relative paths, so the script must run from the repository root.

notes: The README cites the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2024.10.12.617732v2); the peer-reviewed version in Genome Biology (2025) was read instead, through Europe PMC. The paper is CC BY-NC-ND, so its bytes are not stored. The README example sets model_max_length = 1026 for the 4k model; worth a human look before anyone runs long sequences.
